question: The outliner's rows that are not units: CTitleMember, the four battle rows, CAlliedObjectiveMember, the province entry, and the function recorded as BuildOutlinerHeaderTooltip - what each slot does, what each row shows, its tooltip, and what a click does.

structs.name: CCombatMember
structs.comment: **An outliner row for one land battle** (window `outliner_combat_entry`). Built by CCombatMember::CCombatMember from the battle; keeps the battle and its province, an observer glue on `outliner_standard`, and whether the player attacks. Slots: 8 Update, 12 GetKind (1), 13 BuildTooltip, 14 OwnsElement, 15 IsStillCurrent, 16 MarkShown. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
structs.evidence: The constructor at VA 0x6A9B10 writes 0x15D0B3C at [edi] (0x6A9C09) and 0x15D0B84 at [edi+0x1C] (0x6A9C0F); vtable.py CCombatMember shows the slot bodies named here. Size not read, so omitted.

structs.name: CNavalCombatMember
structs.comment: **An outliner row for one sea battle** (window `outliner_combat_entry`). Same layout as CCombatMember to +0x80; +0x84/+0x88 are the two sides' ship counts as last written to the row. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
structs.evidence: The constructor at VA 0x6AAB60 writes 0x15D0C14 at [edi] (0x6AAC59) and 0x15D0C5C at [edi+0x1C] (0x6AAC5F).

structs.name: CAirCombatMember
structs.comment: **An outliner row for one air battle** (window `outliner_combat_entry`). Same layout as CNavalCombatMember; +0x84/+0x88 are the two sides' aircraft. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
structs.evidence: The constructor at VA 0x6AC7A0 writes 0x15D0CEC at [edi] (0x6AC8A8) and 0x15D0D34 at [edi+0x1C] (0x6AC8AE).

structs.name: CBombCombatMember
structs.comment: **An outliner row for one bombing** (window `outliner_combat_entry`), in the section `Our Bombings` or `Hostile Bombing` by its +0x80. It has no Update and no tooltip of its own: slot 8 is the empty stub 0xABF890 and slot 13 EmptyTooltip. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
structs.evidence: The constructor at VA 0x6B50D0 writes 0x15D110C at [edi] (0x6B51CD) and 0x15D1154 at [edi+0x1C] (0x6B51D3); vtable.py CBombCombatMember: slot 8 0xABF890, slot 13 0x776F20 (EmptyTooltip).

structs.name: CAlliedObjectiveMember
structs.comment: **An outliner row for one allied objective** (window `outliner_allied_objective_entry`): a province id and which way the request runs. No Update (slot 8 is 0xABF890), and its MarkShown (slot 16) is the empty 0x60CD50. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
structs.evidence: The constructor at VA 0x6B56E0 writes 0x15D11E4 at [edi] (0x6B57F3) and 0x15D122C at [edi+0x1C] (0x6B57F9).

structs.name: CTitleMember
structs.comment: **An outliner section title** (window `outliner_header_entry`): the section's kind at +0x28 and its name, written once by the constructor through GetOutlinerKindTitle. No count, no tooltip (slot 13 EmptyTooltip), no update (slot 8 0xABF890), no click handler, no expand button. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
structs.evidence: The constructor at VA 0x6ADF10 writes 0x15D1064 at [edi] (0x6AE01D) and 0x15D10AC at [edi+0x1C] (0x6AE023), and makes no observer glue - its only calls after COutLinerMember's constructor are the string assigns, GetOutlinerKindTitle and the text box lookup.

addresses.name: CCombatMember::CCombatMember
addresses.comment: **Makes the outliner row of a land battle.** The battle arrives in ECX and the memory on the stack (`ret 4`). Builds the window `outliner_combat_entry` through COutLinerMember's constructor (0x6A9A30), writes the vftables, keeps the battle (+0x28) and its province (+0x2C), and makes the observer glue whose plain click is CCombatMember::OnClick. **Only when CCombat::GetKind is 1**: the two sides' total strength over 1000 into +0x84/+0x88 (never read), +0x80 = whether the player's id is among the attacker's countries, `entry_text` = CProvince::GetName of the battle's province, the glue attached to `outliner_standard`, then Update. For any other kind +0x28 is zeroed and nothing else is set. Two callers, 0x6A5E99 and 0x6A7AA4. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x6A9B10-0x6A9E88: `mov edi,[ebp+8]; mov esi,ecx` at the head, `ret 4` at 0x6A9E79 and past it the cold block 0x6A9E7C that sets +0x80 to 1 (trap 3); the kind test `call [eax+0x2C]; cmp eax,1` at 0x6A9C52; `outliner_combat_entry`, `entry_text` and `outliner_standard` references at 0x6A9B38, 0x6A9D6C, 0x6A9E11; tail call of 0x6AA840. Wrong if ECX were not the battle - but [esi+0x10]/[esi+0x14]/[esi+0x18] are read as attacker, defender and province, CCombat's recorded fields.

addresses.name: CCombatMember::BuildTooltip
addresses.signature: GuiTooltipText* __thiscall CCombatMember::BuildTooltip(CCombatMember* this, GuiTooltipText* out, CGuiObject* element) @EAX
addresses.comment: **Slot 13: the land battle row's tooltip.** Empty unless the battle is still in its province's combats list and neither side's combatant answers its slot 8 (air) or slot 7 (naval). Key OL_LAND_COMBAT_ATTACK when +0x80 (the player attacks), else OL_LAND_COMBAT_DEFEND, with `ours` the player's side and `theirs` the other. $PROGRESS$ = FormatFixedPoint(CCombat::GetAttackerStrengthShare * 100000 / 1000, **1 decimal**) - the attacker's share as a percentage, truncated to one decimal, **not negated when defending**; $OUR_LEAD$/$THEIR_LEAD$ = the name of CCombatant::GetHighestRankedLeader of the side, or the rendered NO_COMMANDER when that is the null leader; $ENEMY$ = CountryAdjectiveOfTag of the first of theirs' countries still in the fight, or the bare string `NONE` when there is none; $OUR_NUM$/$THEIR_NUM$ = CUnitList::GetTotalNumOfRegiments of the side's front (+0xB0) and $OUR_RES$/$THEIR_RES$ of its reserves (+0xC0). The element is not looked at. `ret 8`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x6A9E90-0x6AA4B3: the province-list walk 0x6A9F18-0x6A9F42; the four combatant slot calls [eax+0x20]/[eax+0x1C] at 0x6A9F48-0x6A9F8A; `cmp byte [ebx+0x80],0` and the swap at 0x6A9FA9-0x6A9FD0; slot 17 then __allmul 0x186A0 / __alldiv 0x3E8 then FormatFixedPoint with `push 1` at 0x6A9FFE-0x6AA04E; the list offsets +0xB0/+0xC0 at 0x6AA32D/0x6AA36D/0x6AA3A9/0x6AA3E5; GuiTooltipText::CopyConstruct into [ebp+8] and `mov eax,ebx` at 0x6AA486-0x6AA4A6.
addresses.revises: Confidence raised from inferred; the out is a GuiTooltipText (CopyConstruct at 0x6AA491), not a Hoi3CString, and the second argument the hovered element; the comment now says what each variable is - PROGRESS is the attacker's strength share, not odds - and that ATTACK/DEFEND follows +0x80.

addresses.name: OutlinerBattleRow_OwnsElement
addresses.comment: **Slot 14 of all four battle rows** (CCombatMember, CNavalCombatMember, CAirCombatMember, CBombCombatMember - the linker folded the four identical bodies): true when the element is the row window's `entry_text`, its `outliner_standard` button or its `info_text`. Which row answers a tooltip. `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x6AA4C0-0x6AA620: three window lookups by name ([win]+0x3C instant text box, +0x34 button) compared with [ebp+8]; vtable.py --holding 0x6AA4C0 lists exactly those four tables at slot 14. Class-free because four sibling classes hold it (trap 4).

addresses.name: CCombatMember::OnClick
addresses.comment: **A click on a land battle's row** (the glue's plain-click handler). If the battle is still in its province's combats list: CInGameIdler::ClearSelection (slot 46), CInGameIdler::Select (slot 38) with the battle's CSelectable (+8) - which opens the battle window through CCombat::OnSelected - and CInGameIdler::CentreOnProvince (slot 48) on the battle's province. No test that it is already open. Bare `ret`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x6AA630-0x6AA839: `[eax+0xB8]` at 0x6AA706, `add edi,8; ... [eax+0x98]` with push edi at 0x6AA713/0x6AA790, `[edx+0xC0]` with [combat+0x18] at 0x6AA819-0x6AA827; the address is the first handler of the glue built at 0x6A9C41.

addresses.name: CCombatMember::Update
addresses.comment: **Slot 8: the land battle row's figure** (`info_text`). If the battle is still in its province: share = CCombat::GetAttackerStrengthShare; the text is `\xA7G` + FormatFixedPoint(share * 100000 / 1000, **0 decimals**) + `%\xA7W` when +0x80 (the player attacks), and `\xA7R` + the same of **-share** when not. So 78 thousandths reads `7%` green to the attacker and `-7%` red to the defender: truncated, whole percent. No cache - rewritten whenever called. Bare `ret`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x6AA840-0x6AAAAC: slot 17 at 0x6AA8AD; `\xA7G` (0x15B5C50) then `cmp byte [edi+0x80],bl; jne` and `neg ecx` with `\xA7R` (0x15B5C58) at 0x6AA8CF-0x6AA8F2; `%\xA7W` (0x15C2148); __allmul 0x186A0, __alldiv 0x3E8 and FormatFixedPoint with `push ebx` (0) at 0x6AA953-0x6AA985; written to `info_text` +0xD0.

addresses.name: CCombatMember::IsStillCurrent
addresses.comment: **Slot 15: whether the row is still wanted.** False unless the battle is still in its province's combats list; then whether it is in the list whose first node is at sets+0x04 (nodes: data +0, next +8). The other three battle rows ask +0x24 (naval), +0x44 (air) and - see CBombCombatMember::IsStillCurrent - +0x04 again. What builds `sets` is the window's (section A). `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x6AAAB0-0x6AAAF3, two `ret 4`. The body is read; the name rests on the reading that sets+4 is the land battles that should be listed, which is section A's to confirm from the caller.

addresses.name: CCombatMember::MarkShown
addresses.comment: **Slot 16: records that the row's battle has a row** - appends a 0x10-byte node {battle, prev, 0, 0} to the list at sets+0x14 (first), +0x18 (last), +0x1C (count). Naval uses +0x34, air +0x54, a bombing +0x74 or +0x94 by its side; the title and the objective row do nothing here. `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x6AAB00-0x6AAB51: operator new(0x10), stores, count increment. The body is read; what the list is used for is the caller's (section A).

addresses.name: CNavalCombatMember::CNavalCombatMember
addresses.comment: **Makes the outliner row of a sea battle.** The battle in ECX, the memory on the stack, `ret 4`. Window `outliner_combat_entry`; battle +0x28, province +0x2C, glue (plain click CNavalCombatMember::OnClick); +0x84 = the attacker's ship count and **+0x88 = the defender's total strength / 1000 truncated** (not a ship count; Update replaces it); +0x80 = the player among the attacker's countries; glue attached to `outliner_standard`; `entry_text` = the province's name; then Update. No test of the battle's kind. Two callers, 0x6A6096 and 0x6A7B56. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.

addresses.name: CAirCombatMember::OnClick
addresses.comment: **A click on an air battle's row - not the land row's**: only if the battle is still in its province **and CCombat::IsLive**, and only if the screen's open battle window (CInGameIdler::GetCombatView, slot 59) is not already this battle: CInGameIdler::DeselectLater(0) (slot 43, where the other rows use ClearSelection), Select the battle, centre the map on its province. A second click on the row of the open battle does nothing. Bare `ret`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x6AD800-0x6ADABD: combat slot 9 ([eax+0x24]) at 0x6AD85D; screen slot 59 ([eax+0xEC]) twice and `cmp [eax+4],edi` at 0x6AD8E7-0x6AD904; `[eax+0xAC]` with push 0 at 0x6AD989; then +0x98 and +0xC0.

addresses.name: CAirCombatMember_GetCombatIfCurrent
addresses.comment: The row's battle (+0x28) if it is still in its province's combats list, else null; the row in EAX. Not a virtual. Called by the window's list code at 0x6A5136, 0x6A52F8 and 0x6A54BA. The class is inferred from where it sits (between CAirCombatMember's OnClick and Update) - the body would serve any battle row. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x6ADAC0-0x6ADADD, bare `ret`; findRefs --callers gives the three sites; vtable.py --holding: in no table. Wrong in its class if those callers walk naval or land rows.

Text `\xA7G` a `\xA7W - \xA7R` d `\xA7W` (player attacks) or `\xA7R` a `\xA7W - \xA7G` d `\xA7W`, rewritten only when a count changes. Bare `ret`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x6ADAE0-0x6ADE52: slot 9 at 0x6ADB42 then 0x5D5CF0 twice, compares at 0x6ADB64/0x6ADB6C, +0x80 at 0x6ADB78.

addresses.name: CTitleMember::CTitleMember
addresses.comment: **Makes an outliner section title.** Window `outliner_header_entry`; kind at +0x28; `entry_text` = GetOutlinerKindTitle(kind), once. No observer glue, no update, nothing else. One caller, 0x6A79E9. `ret 8`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x6ADF10-0x6AE0C8: `outliner_header_entry` at 0x6ADF36, vftables at [edi]/[edi+0x1C], `push [edi+0x28]; push out; call 0x6AE0D0; add esp,8` at 0x6AE03C-0x6AE049, the result written to `entry_text` +0xD0, `ret 8`.

addresses.name: GetOutlinerKindTitle
addresses.comment: **The name of an outliner section, by kind** - not a tooltip and no counts. Renders one localisation key into `out` and answers it: 1 OL_COMBATS (`Land Combat`), 2 OL_NAVAL_COMBAT, 3 OL_AIR_COMBAT, 4 ARMIES (`Land Units`), 5 NAVIES (`Naval Units`), 6 OL_AIR_UNITS, 7 OL_ALLIED_OBJECTIVE (`Allied Objectives`), 8 OL_WE_BOMB (`Our Bombings`), 9 OL_BOMB_ON_US (`Hostile Bombing`); any other kind the empty string. The kinds are the rows' GetKind (slot 12) values. Three callers: CTitleMember::CTitleMember (0x6AE044), the configuration list (0x6A301F) and the window (0x6A86CC). Five bare `ret`s, `mov eax,ebx` before each. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x6AE0D0-0x6AE5F4: `mov eax,[ebp+0xC]; mov ebx,[ebp+8]`, the compare chain `cmp eax,1/2/3/4/5/6/9/8/7`, a key string per arm, CInternationalizedText::Render into ebx, `mov eax,ebx` at 0x6AE1BC; callers `push kind; push out; call; add esp,8` at 0x6A3017-0x6A3024 and 0x6AE03C-0x6AE049.
addresses.revises: Renamed from BuildOutlinerHeaderTooltip: it is the title text of a section, by kind, and not a tooltip of counts. The placeholder signature `void __cdecl (void)` is replaced by the two arguments read off the callers, and the invalid confidence `likely` by confirmed.

addresses.name: CTitleMember::GetKind
addresses.comment: Slot 12, `mov eax, 0xB; ret`: a title's own kind is 11, outside the 1-9 of the rows it heads. The row kinds, all slot 12: CCombatMember 1, CNavalCombatMember 2, CAirCombatMember 3, CArmyMember 4, CNavyMember 5, CAirMember 6 (the folded Return_N bodies), CAlliedObjectiveMember 7, CBombCombatMember 8 or 9. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Bytes at 0x6AE600: `B8 0B 00 00 00 C3`; vtable.py --holding 0x6AE600: CTitleMember slot 12 only.

addresses.name: CTitleMember::OwnsElement
addresses.comment: Slot 14: true when the element is the title window's `entry_text`, or its `outliner_standard` button - which `outliner_header_entry` does not have, so in practice the text alone. `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x6AE610-0x6AE70A, `ret 4`; the two name lookups. The header window in interface/outliner.gui declares only the icon `outliner_header` and `entry_text`.

addresses.name: CTitleMember_GetKindField
addresses.comment: `mov eax,[eax+0x28]; ret` - the row's +0x28, the row in EAX. Sits right after CTitleMember::OwnsElement, which is why it is given to the title (+0x28 = its kind); the body would read any row's +0x28. Called by the window's list code at 0x6A7F9B, 0x6A824E and 0x6A8588. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Bytes at 0x6AE710 `8B 40 28 C3` between three int3 above and twelve below; findRefs --callers gives the three sites; in no virtual table. Wrong in its class if those callers hand it battle rows.

addresses.name: CBombCombatMember::CBombCombatMember
addresses.comment: **Makes the outliner row of a bombing.** Window `outliner_combat_entry`; bombing +0x28, province +0x2C, glue (plain click CBombCombatMember::OnClick); +0x80 = the player among the bombing side's (attacker's) countries; `entry_text` = the province's name; glue attached to `outliner_standard`. **`info_text` is never written** - the row shows no figure - and there is no Update to write one. Two callers, 0x6A6B4A and 0x6A6D48. `ret 8`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x6B50D0-0x6B53A8: [ebp+8]/[ebp+0xC], `outliner_combat_entry` 0x6B50F9, `entry_text` 0x6B52AA, `outliner_standard` 0x6B534B, no `info_text` reference in the body (the string's twelve references in the image are all elsewhere); slot 8 of the table is 0xABF890.

addresses.name: CBombCombatMember::GetKind
addresses.comment: Slot 12: `8 + (this->player_bombs == 0)` - 8 `Our Bombings` when the player is the bombing side, 9 `Hostile Bombing` when not. **Abuts CBombCombatMember::OnClick with one int3** (trap 2). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Bytes 0x6B53C0-0x6B53CE: `xor eax,eax; cmp [ecx+0x80],al; sete al; add eax,8; ret`; one int3 at 0x6B53CF.

addresses.name: CBombCombatMember::OnClick
addresses.comment: A click on a bombing's row: if it is still its province's bombing (CMapProvince +0x2FC), ClearSelection, Select it (which opens the bombing's window) and centre the map on its province. Bare `ret`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x6B53D0-0x6B55BD: `[eax+0x2FC]` at 0x6B53EE, screen slots +0xB8, +0x98 (edi = bombing+8 at 0x6B5497), +0xC0; the glue's handler in the constructor.

addresses.name: CBombCombatMember::GetCombatIfCurrent
addresses.comment: The row's bombing if it is still its province's bombing (+0x2FC), else null - branch-free (`setne; dec; and`). Not a virtual. Called by the window's list code at 0x6A567C and 0x6A583E. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Bytes 0x6B55C0-0x6B55D4, bare `ret`; findRefs --callers gives the two sites. The class from where it sits, between the bombing row's OnClick and slot 15, and from its +0x2FC read, which only the bombing row's slots make.

addresses.name: CBombCombatMember::IsStillCurrent
addresses.comment: Slot 15: false unless the row's bombing is still its province's bombing (+0x2FC); then whether it is in the list at **sets+0x04 - the same list CCombatMember::IsStillCurrent asks**, where the other battle rows ask their own (+0x24, +0x44) and MarkShown writes the bombings to +0x74/+0x94. Read as written; what +0x04 holds is the window's (section A). `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x6B55E0-0x6B5614: `cmp edx,[eax+0x2FC]`, then `mov ecx,[ebp+8]; mov eax,[ecx+4]` at 0x6B55F7-0x6B55FA.

addresses.name: CBombCombatMember::MarkShown
addresses.comment: Slot 16: appends the bombing to the list at sets+0x74 when the player is bombed (+0x80 = 0), +0x94 when the player bombs. `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x6B5620-0x6B56D2: `cmp [this+0x80],0` and the two lists +0x74..+0x7C and +0x94..+0x9C.

addresses.name: CAlliedObjectiveMember::CAlliedObjectiveMember

addresses.name: CAlliedObjectiveMember::BuildTooltip
addresses.signature: GuiTooltipText* __thiscall CAlliedObjectiveMember::BuildTooltip(CAlliedObjectiveMember* this, GuiTooltipText* out, CGuiObject* element) @EAX
addresses.comment: **Slot 13: the objective's sentence.** Asked of the player (+0x80): for each record of CGameState +0xB9C[player] whose province is the row's, the countries that asked, each `\xA7Y` name `\xA7W` (CountryNameOfCountry), `, ` between and ` ` + AND + ` ` before the last; then OL_AO_THEY_REQUEST (` have requested that we`). Asked by the player: OL_AO_WE_REQUEST (`We have requested that `) and the countries of the +0xBAC[player] record, listed the same way. Then OL_AO_DEFEND (` defend near `, green) when the faction of the province's **controller** is the player's faction, else OL_AO_ATTACK (` attack near `, red), and `\xA7Y` province name `\xA7W.`. `ret 8`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x6B5A40-0x6B6892: the +0x80 branch at 0x6B5B2D with +0xB9C at 0x6B5B3A and +0xBAC at 0x6B62AF; the record compare `cmp eax,[edx+0x28]` at 0x6B5B7B; the list loop 0x6B5C20-0x6B5E02 with ` ` / AND / ` ` (0x6B5C3A, 0x6B5C46, 0x6B5D75) for the last and `, ` (0x6B5D88) otherwise; `lea ecx,[ecx+0x334]` (controller) then CCountryTag::GetCountry and `+0xD8` (faction) against the player's at 0x6B5F78-0x6B5FA4; OL_AO_DEFEND 0x6B5FB0, OL_AO_ATTACK 0x6B60DE, `\xA7W.` 0x6B6286.

The argument is not used. `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::CentreOnProvinceId
addresses.comment: Slot 47 of the in-game screen: CentreOnProvince (slot 48) on the game state's province array (+0xB8C) at the id. `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-outliner.md, section C.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x64C020-0x64C0DC: `mov ecx,[esi+0xB8C]; mov edx,[ebp+8]; mov ecx,[ecx+edx*4]` then `call [eax+0xC0]` on this; vtable.py --holding 0x64C020: CInGameIdler slot 47 only.

slots_noted: Slot 0 of the five battle and objective rows is the deleting destructor 0x6ACB50, folded across 13 tables (CCombatEntry, CBookmarkEntry, CConvoyProvinceEntry and others), left unnamed (trap 4). Stubs in the recorded slots: 8 = 0xABF890 (empty) for CTitleMember, CBombCombatMember, CAlliedObjectiveMember; 13 = EmptyTooltip for CTitleMember and CBombCombatMember; 15 = 0xB129A0 (`mov al,1; ret 4`, 37 tables) for CTitleMember; 16 = 0x60CD50 (`ret 4`) for CTitleMember and CAlliedObjectiveMember; 12 = Return_1/2/3 for the three battle rows.
